title: Choose the landing page structure
question: Three structures for the Hindsight landing page, all in the app's existing graphite-and-board world. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: PGN in, review out
options.thesis: The first viewport is the transformation: raw PGN text flows in from the left, becomes a board, and leaves as annotated moves.
options.viewport: Headline with the username/PGN input inline; below, one full-width band where the Opera Game's PGN streams into a board and out as Mistake / Brilliant / Blunder lines.
options.risk: If the band reads as three panels instead of one flow, it collapses into a split hero.

raised.raise: The input is the hero's own control: you type into the headline row, not a button below it.

options.label: Tournament wall chart
options.thesis: The page is a pairing wall of famous games already reviewed; your game claims Board 1.
options.viewport: A ruled grid fills the screen: a double-size Board 1 cell holds the input, surrounded by famous games each showing both accuracies and their key badges, each one clickable into a real review.
options.risk: Famous-game accuracies must come from real reviews we run, never invented numbers; the grid can feel like a dashboard.

options.label: The game plays itself
options.thesis: A giant board replays the Opera Game on load with badges popping, eval bar swinging and the coach talking; the input docks on the board like a player bar.
options.viewport: An 820px board centred under the fold line, eval bar at its edge, a Brilliant badge landing on b5, the coach line beside it, and the username input floating across the board's lower rank.
options.risk: Closest to what Chess.com itself shows; the motion has to carry it or it reads as a screenshot.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Pages keyed by number on a 40×24 grid.
options.viewport: P100 index with the game list as numbered pages.
options.case: Loses both axes: players don't recognise a review in it.
options.kept: The input is the whole interface.

options.label: Streaming title wall
options.thesis: Recent games as poster rows that expand on focus.
options.viewport: Rows of game tiles; the focused one shows its accuracy.
options.risk: Needs a username before it shows anything.
options.case: Loses clarity for a first-time visitor with no games loaded.
options.kept: One focused item grows; everything else steps back.

options.label: Multiplane cel dawn
options.thesis: Painted depth layers sliding at different speeds.
options.viewport: A painted forest with the product name on the nearest cel.
options.risk: A picture of a world, not a chess tool.
options.kept: Depth by layered speed, used for the board's pieces.

options.label: Miura-fold sheet
options.thesis: One pull deploys a whole creased field.
options.viewport: A packet unfolding into the review.
options.kept: One action unfolds everything at once.

options.label: Suminagashi ink basin
options.thesis: The page as a fluid surface you stir.
options.viewport: A basin of marbled ink answering the pointer.
options.risk: GPU cost and no product in sight.
options.kept: The newest mark is always the darkest.

options.label: Raygun layout desk
options.thesis: Colliding columns you feel before you read.
options.risk: Illegible where clarity is the product.
options.kept: The urgent fragment is allowed to break the grid.
